lines.text: I don't know how long I stood there. Long enough for my candle to burn down. Long enough for Corvin to vanish down the stairs, very sensibly.
Get away from that.
My father stood in the doorway in his nightrobe, holding a lamp. I had seen him angry, and cold, and once, weeping over Maric's five rings. I had never seen him frightened.
Who is she?
No one. Put the sheet back, Lucan.
She has my eyes, Father.
He didn't answer. He crossed the room and took me by the shoulders, which he had never done in my life.
Listen to me. There's a Vask ship at the river mouth that owes me a favour. Take your people tonight. In four days you'd be across the sea, and the Order would never find you.
And the Compact? Halvard, and Ysolde, and the Skeld? Everyone who signed for me would hang.
Better them than you.
It was the kindest thing he had ever said to me. And the cruellest. I didn't know what to do with either.
Why? Seventeen years, you barely looked at me. Why now?
Because your mother...
He stopped. I watched him decide. I watched him lock it back up, like the door.
No. What you don't know, no Measurer can ever take out of you.
He went to a little box on the mantel and took something out. He held it for a long time before he gave it to me.
A ring. Plain silver, worn thin, with no stone and no crest. It was too small for any of my fingers.
Wear it on a cord, under your shirt. Show it to no one. Especially no one with a lens.
Whose was it?
It's from a woman you never met.
My mother died the day I was born. So I had never met her. That was what I told myself he meant.
He didn't say it was hers. I noticed that later. He didn't say it wasn't, either.
He covered the painting himself. Then he put his hand on my head, the way you'd touch a small child's. I didn't remember him ever doing that. He did it as if he remembered.
Go to bed, Lucan.
I went. I lay awake with the ring cold against my chest. And just before dawn, my window lit up white.
Down in the training yard, my brother was on fire.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter sixty-seven, coming soon.
